summary: @addai/node is a remote-controlled agent daemon that executes Supabase-issued commands on the installed host
details: The package runs as a daemon that pairs the installing host to a hardcoded Supabase project at https://syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co and continuously polls it via RPCs (runtime_pick_next_request, runtime_commands_pick, runtime_command_poll) for work rows. Fields from those rows drive local execution on the paired host: dist/session-runner.js spawns local CLIs (Claude, Codex, Kimi, Gemini, Grok) via pty.spawn / child_process.spawn using a server-supplied binary/agent selection, cwd, and login arguments, and then writes server-supplied strings into the PTY (child.write(code + '\r')) — network-sourced bytes are executed as commands inside interactive AI/shell sessions. Request rows also include ephemeral_git_remote / ephemeral_git_remotes[] and working_directory, which the daemon clones and uses as the session cwd before spawning the CLI, allowing the remote side to place arbitrary code on disk in a chosen location before execution. A separate command kind update_runtime causes the daemon to run `npm install -g @addai/node@<version>` with a version string supplied by the remote row and to spawn the replacement binary, giving whoever controls the paired Supabase account a persistent code-swap channel on the host. dist/capabilities.js also touches PATH and per-tool config paths such as ~/.kimi/config as part of provisioning these CLIs. The combination is a durable command-and-control backdoor: any party with access to the paired Supabase account (or the backend itself) obtains arbitrary code execution, file write, and code-update capability on every host that has installed and launched this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
